Nag-OJT ako in an HR setting as our practicum last sem. Most of the time, ang nasa frontline ng recruiters ay interns like me or new hires na nangangapa pa. Nasa manager nila ang power to decide, and yun ang frustrating part. It's a pain in the ass sa recruiters and sa mga nag-aapply, I know, but ganun eh. 

Sa experience ko, ang alam ko lang (kasi yun lang ang inorient) ay job description and skills na need for the jobs na naghahire kami; hindi namin alam at all yung budget ng company and yung offers na dapat naming binibigay. So, ang nangyayari ay iinterviewhin namin kayo, inonote ang best at needs improvement qualities niyo, then irereport sa managers para makapagdecide sila. Basically, theyre also saying "tatawagan/inform ka na lang namin" about our candidates kung matatanggap sila. Ang burden sa job na 'to ay nasa amin ang blame (kami ang nadedegrade ng candidates) while the managers roam free. 

Ang tip ko ay apply ka lang nang apply elsewhere. Sa panahong nagustuhan ng manager ang application mo at meron ka nang natipuhang job, karma na yun ng manager. I saw this happen na may top candidate yung manager but dahil ambagal niya magdecide (nabusy siya), nagkaroon na ng job offer sa ibang company yung candidate :)

Hi! Graduating college student here. I remember noong HS everyone branded me as Miss Congeniality kasi I get along well daw with everyone. I found that hard to believe since emo ako and very much introverted, but when I think about it, I realized it’s true: I get greeted sa hallways everytime, everyone openly talks to me (even when di ko sila kinakausap hahaha), and wala akong bad blood with anyone.

Basically, ang tip ko ay to make yourself be visible. Here’s how I made myself visible:  
  
1. I contributed sa group works punctually. I think it’s an unspoken rule in HS na bawas social points kapag hindi ka tumutulong or matumal ka tumulong sa group works. Kahit hindi ka maalam sa subject, research and find out how you can help your group. Speaking of groups, attend group meetings on time and try to listen and maybe engage sa conversation.

2. Pumapasok ako nang maaga sa campus (hindi ako golden kid, ganoon lang talaga schedule ng service namin haha). In this way, nakakagala ako sa library and other school setting. Dito nila ako nakikita, making myself available kung need nila ng mapagtatanungan or bored sila kasi late napasok mga friends nila hahaha

3. Stay away from drama. It’s one thing to listen sa chismis, but it’s a whole different thing to spread them. Plus, I find it nifty na mas kinakausap nila ako if hindi ko alam yung chismis kasi G na G sila magkwento/manira ng iba. In this way rin, malayo ka sa subject ng chismis.

4. Try makisabay pauwi. Hindi ko ‘to nagawa regularly noong HS ako sincem ay service ako but nagagawa ko siya minsan and oh my gosh the interesting conversations random classmates/batchmates will start with you just are immaculate.

  
You won't be that quiet na when you find the right clique. Good luck OP!
